assessment.nobel_worthiness: The detection of a diffuse flux of astrophysical neutrinos at TeV-PeV energies opened a genuinely new window on the universe, and the discovery is read straight from nature rather than from a model. It is a clear, self-contained discovery that fits the committee's habit of putting the discovery first. The existential and cosmic-ray-origin questions it addresses are of broad interest.
assessment.attribution: The credited list has two names, so a fair configuration is easy. Halzen conceived and led IceCube and Karle was central to its construction and early analysis; as I understand it, the discovery paper is a collaboration result, so the committee would have to decide whether the instrument leaders are the right people, and a third person such as a detector-construction leader may be arguable but is not in the supplied credit.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed independently by multiple analysis channels, and followed by the TXS 0506+056 coincidence and evidence from NGC 1068, so the central claim is stable. Source identification is still incomplete, but the discovery itself is mature and timely.
uncertainties: Exact personal credit within a large collaboration; I have not independently verified the roles of Karle and Halzen.
Origin of the diffuse flux remains only partly resolved, so the prize would be for the detection and the instrument rather than for source identification.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Resolving the shadow of a supermassive black hole at horizon scale is a direct clue from nature about strong-field gravity, and the images of M87* and Sgr A* matter greatly to anyone who works on black holes and gravity. The result is vivid, clear and has lasting impact, though the 2020 prize already honoured black-hole physics in other forms.
assessment.attribution: Falcke proposed the shadow-imaging idea, Doeleman led the building of the global VLBI array and Zensus was a leader in the European VLBI effort; these are plausible, but the work is by a collaboration of hundreds, and the allocation among them is not obviously fair. A prize for individuals rather than the collaboration would be contested.
assessment.maturity: Two independent targets and several observing epochs, with consistency with general relativity at the roughly ten percent level. The interpretation is stable but precision tests of alternatives (e.g. horizonless mimickers) remain limited; recognition is timely but could ripen.
uncertainties: Collaboration-scale credit makes the attribution fragile.
Tests of the Kerr shadow are still coarse, so strong-field conclusions are modest.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The optical lattice clock, built on Katori's magic-wavelength idea, reached uncertainties near 1e-18 and underlies the coming redefinition of the second and tests of fundamental constants and gravitational redshift. It is a decisive, important and original invention with large and lasting impact.
assessment.attribution: The credit is a compact pair: Katori invented the concept and Ye developed the strontium clock to the highest precision. The two-name configuration is natural, though the 2005 prize (Hall, Hansch) for frequency combs and trapped-ion clock work from Wineland's 2012 prize touch neighbouring ground, and other groups (e.g. Lemonde, Gill) might be argued for.
assessment.maturity: Many independent clocks worldwide agree, so the technology is very mature. Timing is good given the pending redefinition of the second.
uncertainties: Overlap with earlier clock and comb prizes may reduce the sense of novelty for some members.
Contributions of other clock groups are not in the supplied credit.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Precision measurement of the acoustic peaks and the CMB anisotropy spectrum fixed the standard cosmological model, including the need for dark energy, which is close to my own field. It is a result extracted from nature with enormous impact; but the prize for COBE (2006) and for physical cosmology (2019) already cover much of the ground.
assessment.attribution: Five names are credited, so the committee must cut to three. WMAP leadership (Bennett, Page, Spergel) is the most natural trio, but Puget (Planck/Archeops) and Sunyaev (theory of the acoustic signature and the SZ effect) are strong cases, and boomerang-type balloon groups are missing from the list. The allocation is genuinely unresolved.
assessment.maturity: Fully mature: WMAP and Planck agree, and the standard model has been checked many times. The doubt is novelty relative to earlier prizes rather than maturity.
uncertainties: Credit is spread over experiments and theory, and the three chosen names leave out important contributors.
Possible redundancy with the 2006 and 2019 prizes.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The prediction and observation of the quantum spin Hall effect and of topological insulators reshaped condensed-matter physics and gave a new classification of matter, in the line of the 2016 topology prize. It combines a clean theoretical idea with decisive experiment.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele made the decisive theoretical proposal; Molenkamp's group observed the quantum spin Hall state in HgTe quantum wells following the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang prediction. The omission of Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang, and of the three-dimensional experimental work, in this credit is a fair concern; I rely only on the supplied names.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed in many materials and platforms, and the theory is stable. Recognition is mature and plausible.
uncertainties: Competing credit for the HgTe prediction and 3D topological insulators is not captured in this entry.
Near-duplicate of B062, which suggests the committee should settle the framing.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Conformal field theory of two-dimensional critical phenomena is a deep foundation for statistical physics and for string theory, which I know well. Unlike some purely formal results it has been confirmed against exactly solved and experimental critical systems, so it is not unconfirmed speculation.
assessment.attribution: BPZ is a natural trio, with Zamolodchikov the late member; the Nobel statutes forbid posthumous awards, and I believe Zamolodchikov (A. B.) is alive, though I have not verified this. Friedan, Shenker and Cardy are also candidates for credit, which complicates the allocation.
assessment.maturity: Decades of confirmation; timing is certainly not premature, and the case is overdue rather than early.
uncertainties: Whether the committee views this as sufficiently tied to experiment rather than mathematical physics.
Allocation relative to Cardy, Friedan, Shenker and others.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Kilonova theory, confirmed by AT2017gfo after GW170817, links neutron-star mergers to heavy-element nucleosynthesis and answers where much of the gold comes from. The finding has strong existential resonance and strong confirmation from nature.
assessment.attribution: The prize would honour theorists who predicted the transient, but the observational discovery rests on LIGO/Virgo and multi-telescope teams, and the 2017 prize already honoured gravitational waves. Allocation among Metzger, Kasen, Lattimer, Foley and the original Li-Paczynski proposal is unresolved.
assessment.maturity: A single well-observed event dominates the evidence, with later candidates less clear, so confirmation is real but thin.
uncertainties: Evidence rests on one dominant event.
Credit omits the originators and the observers.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The prediction of flat bands at the magic angle and the observation of correlated insulators and superconductivity in twisted bilayer graphene opened an entire field. It is original and has high impact, but I would weigh the fast pace of change and unsettled microscopic mechanism.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald made the theoretical prediction and Jarillo-Herrero's group made the decisive experimental discovery, so the trio is coherent. The key experimental credit may also touch other groups, which is not reflected here.
assessment.maturity: Reproduced by many labs, but the mechanism of the superconductivity is still debated, so recognition may be somewhat early.
uncertainties: Pairing mechanism and many correlated states remain uncertain.
Possible premature timing compared with older candidates.
